tool.name: ESMFold Batch
tool.description: predict structures for multiple FASTA records in one run
tool.command: #set $execution_mode_arg = "" #if $execution_mode.mode == "cpu_only": #set $execution_mode_arg = "--cpu-only" #elif $execution_mode.mode == "cpu_offload": #set $execution_mode_arg = "--cpu-offload" #end if #set $max_tokens_arg = "" #if $advanced.max_tokens_per_batch.mode == "custom": #set $max_tokens_arg = "--max-tokens-per-batch '%s'" % $advanced.max_tokens_per_batch.value #end if #set $chunk_size_arg = "" #if $advanced.chunk_size.mode == "custom": #set $chunk_size_arg = "--chunk-size '%s'" % $advanced.chunk_size.value #end if #set $archive_arg = "" #if str($save_all_outputs) == "true": #set $archive_arg = "--output-archive 'esmfold_batch_all_outputs.zip'" #end if #set $esmfold_command_arg = "" #if str($esmfold_command) not in ["", "None"]: #set $esmfold_command_arg = "--esmfold-command '%s'" % $esmfold_command #end if python '$__tool_directory__/run_esmfold_batch.py' --input-fasta '$sequences' --structures-dir 'batch_structures' --summaries-dir 'batch_summaries' --combined-summary-json 'combined_summary.json' --run-log 'run_log.txt' $archive_arg $esmfold_command_arg --num-recycles '$num_recycles' $execution_mode_arg $max_tokens_arg $chunk_size_arg
tool.help:
ESMFold Batch accepts a multi-FASTA file and runs the official ``esm-fold`` CLI once for all records. It organizes outputs for downstream batch processing:
- ``structure models``: a collection of PDB structures - ``per-record summaries``: a collection of JSON summary files - ``combined summary``: one JSON file listing all records and metrics - ``run log``: plain-text status log with START/SUCCESS/FAILED lines - optional ``complete output archive``: the raw esm-fold directory plus the organized structures and summaries
Records are run one at a time so a failed sequence is recorded as ``failed`` and does not block later sequences. Successful records still produce PDB outputs. Within a single running job, existing per-record outputs are skipped if found. After a Galaxy job is killed and resubmitted, Galaxy usually starts a fresh job working directory, so full cross-job resume depends on an external persistent working directory.
If you want Galaxy-level retry and scheduling for each sequence, use the single-sequence ESMFold tool with a dataset collection instead. This batch tool is better when you want one large job and one organized result folder.
